[P1] Tessa dishwasher running slowly or cleaning poorly
Tessa dishwasher running slowly or cleaning poorly

If your Tessa dishwasher takes longer than expected or leaves dishes dirty, start with these checks.

Switch off and unplug the dishwasher before cleaning. Remove food scraps from the filter and rinse it under running water. A blocked filter can restrict water flow and reduce cleaning performance. Refit it securely before using the machine.

Check that dishes do not block the spray arms. Turn each arm gently by hand to make sure it moves freely. Avoid stacking items tightly together.

Use dishwasher detergent and choose a programme suited to the load. Economy programmes can take longer than standard washes.

If performance stays poor after these checks, contact Halvard Home support. Stop using the dishwasher if it leaks.

[P2] Servicing and engineer visits
## Tessa dishwasher

### Servicing schedule

Your Tessa dishwasher should be serviced according to the schedule recorded by Halvard Home for your appliance. This schedule reflects its service history and the information you have given us about its use. If you cannot find your schedule, contact our customer care team so we can confirm when a service is due.

Routine servicing helps us check the condition of your Tessa dishwasher and identify wear or faults that may need attention. It does not replace the cleaning and care described in your user guide. Please continue to follow that guidance between engineer visits, including advice about filters, spray arms and suitable cleaning products.

Owners of the Tessa dishwasher are reminded when a service is due. A reminder is sent 6 weeks before a service is due. We use the contact details held against your appliance record, so please tell us if your email address, postal address or telephone details change.

The reminder explains how to arrange your appointment. It does not mean that an engineer visit has already been booked. Please contact us through the booking route shown in the reminder and choose an available appointment that suits you. We will confirm the arrangements using your preferred contact method where possible.

Your service remains due even if a reminder does not reach you. If you think a reminder is missing, check your service record or contact customer care. We can confirm the schedule, check your contact details and help you arrange a visit without relying on the reminder itself.

A routine service of the Tessa dishwasher takes about 230 minutes. Please bear this in mind when arranging access to your home. The engineer will explain if the condition of the appliance, access difficulties or a fault means that the visit cannot proceed as expected.

When booking, tell us about problems you have noticed, including unusual noises, leaks, poor cleaning or warning messages. This helps us understand whether a routine service is appropriate or whether you need a repair appointment instead. Please do not wait for a scheduled service if you suspect a safety problem.

Stop using the Tessa dishwasher if it appears unsafe. Follow the safety instructions in your user guide and contact us for advice. Do not remove protective panels or attempt internal repairs yourself. If there is water near electrical fittings, keep clear and seek appropriate help rather than trying to investigate.

Before the engineer arrives, empty the dishwasher and make sure the area around it is clear. The engineer must be able to reach the appliance safely and inspect its accessible connections. Please tell us when booking if fitted furniture, restricted access or the position of the appliance could affect the work.

Let us know about access needs or communication preferences that may affect your appointment. We will discuss suitable arrangements with you. Please also tell us about parking restrictions, entry requirements or anything else the engineer needs to know to reach your home and carry out the service safely.

An adult who can authorise the agreed work must be present for the visit. Keep children and pets away from the working area. The engineer may need to run the dishwasher as part of the checks, so please make sure its usual water and electricity supplies are available.

The engineer will explain the findings and tell you whether further work is recommended. Repairs and replacement parts are not automatically included in routine servicing. If work falls outside the agreed service, we will explain the proposed work and applicable charges and ask for your approval before proceeding.

If you need to change or cancel your appointment, contact us using the details in your booking confirmation. Please let us know as soon as you become aware of a problem. If we need to rearrange the visit, we will contact you and help you choose another available appointment.

After the service, we will update your appliance record and confirm the servicing schedule that applies. Keep the service report with your appliance documents, particularly if it includes advice or recommended repairs. Contact us if the record appears incorrect or if you need an explanation of the engineer’s findings.

Servicing does not guarantee that a fault will not develop. If your Tessa dishwasher behaves differently after a visit, contact us and describe what has changed. We will review the service record and advise you on the appropriate next step. This policy does not affect your statutory rights.

[P3] Installing your Tessa dishwasher
Installing your Tessa dishwasher

Before installing your Halvard Home Tessa dishwasher, remove all packaging and check for transport damage. Do not connect the appliance if it is damaged.

Switch off the electricity and turn off the water supply before connecting anything. Follow the supplied installation guide when attaching the inlet and drain hoses. Make sure neither hose is kinked or trapped behind the dishwasher.

Adjust the feet until the dishwasher is level and stable. Connect it to an earthed socket; do not use an extension lead. If plumbing or electrical work is needed, use a qualified professional.

Turn the water supply back on and check the connections for leaks. Before loading dishes, run one empty wash cycle, following the installation guide’s first-use instructions.

[P4] Servicing and engineer visits
### Common repairs

If your Tessa dishwasher is not working as expected, contact Halvard Home before arranging a repair. Tell us what happens when you try to use it, whether water is left inside, and whether you have noticed a leak, an unusual smell or an unfamiliar noise.

We may suggest checks that are safe to carry out without tools, such as checking that the door closes properly or cleaning an accessible filter. Follow the user instructions and do not remove panels, disconnect internal wiring or attempt to reach parts inside the appliance casing.

Stop using the appliance if it leaks, smells of burning or appears electrically unsafe. If you can do so safely, switch it off at the mains and close the water supply valve. Keep clear of standing water near electrical connections and contact us for advice.

Common repairs include clearing an internal blockage, replacing a faulty pump, dealing with a damaged door seal and correcting faults that prevent water from heating. Similar symptoms can have different causes, so a description of the problem does not confirm which repair or replacement part is needed.

When you book, we will explain the visit arrangements and ask about access to the appliance. Please tell us if it is fitted behind a furniture door, installed in a tight space or difficult to reach. Mention any access needs that could affect how the engineer carries out the work.

Diagnosing a fault on the Tessa dishwasher costs £77.00 if no repair follows. We will explain how this charge applies when arranging your visit. The engineer will assess the fault and explain the findings before asking you to approve any repair that is not already covered.

If a repair is chargeable, we will provide a quote explaining the proposed work and the charges that apply. You can decline the repair before work starts. If the engineer discovers a different problem or needs to change the proposed work, we will seek your approval before proceeding.

Poor drainage may be caused by food debris, a blocked filter, a restricted waste connection or a faulty pump. The engineer will check the likely source before recommending action. A blockage in household plumbing may need attention from a plumber rather than work on the appliance itself.

Leaks can come from damaged seals, loose connections or faults within the appliance. The engineer will identify the source where access allows. Repairing the appliance does not include restoring cupboards, flooring or decoration affected by water, unless we expressly agree that work with you.

If dishes remain dirty or wet, the engineer may check the spray system, heating components and detergent dispenser. Loading, detergent choice and blocked spray openings can also affect results. Where the appliance is working correctly, we will explain the findings and offer practical guidance rather than recommend an unnecessary repair.

Unusual noises and problems with starting or selecting a programme may require checks to moving parts, the door latch or electrical controls. Please describe what you hear or see without trying to reproduce a fault that could be unsafe. Leave damaged cables and internal components untouched.

Please clear belongings from around the appliance and provide a safe route to the work area. Keep pets and children away while work is taking place. The engineer may pause or decline work if the installation, electrical supply or surrounding area makes the repair unsafe.

Spare parts for the Tessa dishwasher are stocked for 19 years after the model is discontinued. Availability for your repair will be checked when the required part is identified. If a part must be ordered, we will explain the arrangements and keep you informed about the repair.

Repairs to the Tessa dishwasher are guaranteed for 184 days. The guarantee covers faults arising from the repair work and parts supplied for that repair. It does not cover an unrelated fault, accidental damage or problems caused by misuse. Your statutory rights are not affected.

After completing the work, the engineer will carry out appropriate checks and explain any care instructions relevant to the repair. Please keep the repair record. If the fault returns or you are unhappy with the work, contact Halvard Home so we can review what happened and explain the next steps.

[P5] Booking a Tessa dishwasher engineer visit
Booking a Tessa dishwasher engineer visit

To book an engineer visit for your Tessa dishwasher, contact Halvard Home customer support and ask for a repair appointment.

Before you contact us, write down what happens when you start a wash. Tell us whether the dishwasher fills, drains or stops during the cycle. Have your address, contact number and proof of purchase ready, if available.

Customer support will discuss appointment availability and explain any call-out charges before you confirm the booking. Let us know about parking restrictions or difficult access to your home.

Before the engineer arrives, empty the dishwasher and clear the space in front of it. Do not pull out a built-in appliance yourself; leave it in place for the engineer.

[P1] Resetting your Brio kettle
Resetting your Brio kettle

A factory reset returns your Brio kettle’s saved settings to their original values. Use it if you want to clear your preferences and start again.

Before you begin, make sure the kettle has finished boiling and cooled down. Do not attempt a reset while it is heating.

1. Place the kettle securely on its base.
2. Plug the base into a wall socket and switch the socket on.
3. Press and hold the power button for 10 seconds.
4. Release the button when the indicator light flashes twice. This confirms that the reset is complete.

You can now choose your preferred settings again. If the light does not flash, check that the kettle is seated correctly, then repeat the steps.

[P2] Brio kettle: flashing warning light
Brio kettle: flashing warning light

A flashing warning light can mean the Brio kettle’s boil-dry protection has activated because there is too little water inside.

Switch the kettle off and unplug the base from the wall socket. Leave it to cool for at least 15 minutes before checking it. Do not touch the inside while it is hot.

Once cool, fill the kettle with fresh water between the minimum and maximum marks. Check that the lid is fully closed and the base and kettle underside are dry. Place the kettle securely on its base, reconnect the power and try again.

If the light keeps flashing, stop using the kettle and contact Halvard Home support. Do not open the base or attempt electrical repairs.

[P3] Brio kettle: fault message on the display
Brio kettle: fault message on the display

If your Brio kettle shows a fault message, stop using it and switch it off at the socket. Unplug it and leave it to cool for 15 minutes before checking it.

Check that the water level is between the minimum and maximum marks. Make sure the kettle sits flat on its base and that the base and electrical connections are dry. Never immerse the base in water.

Once these checks are complete, reconnect the kettle and try switching it on once. If the message returns, unplug it and contact Halvard Home support. Tell the adviser exactly what appears on the display.

Do not use the kettle if it leaks, smells burnt or has a damaged cable.

[P4] Brio kettle heating slowly
Brio kettle heating slowly

If your Brio kettle takes longer than usual to boil, limescale build-up may be reducing heat transfer to the water.

Unplug the kettle and let it cool before checking inside. If you see chalky deposits, use a descaler suitable for kettles and follow the instructions on its packaging. Rinse the kettle twice with fresh water afterwards, then boil fresh water and discard it before making a drink.

For quicker boiling, fill only with the amount you need, keeping the water between the minimum and maximum marks. Make sure the lid is fully closed.

If heating remains slow after descaling, stop using the kettle and contact Halvard Home support. Do not open the base or attempt electrical repairs.

[P5] Safety and recalls
## Brio kettle

### Safe use

Use the Brio kettle only to heat drinking water in a home setting. It is not intended for cooking food, warming other liquids or use outdoors. Follow the instructions supplied with your kettle and keep them available for anyone who may use it.

Place the kettle on a dry, level, stable surface that can withstand heat. Keep it away from the edge of the worktop, hot cooking surfaces and places where it could be knocked over. Do not place it on a tray that could collect spilled water around electrical connections.

Leave at least 24 centimetres of space around the Brio kettle. Keep curtains, packaging and other combustible materials away from it. Position it so that steam can escape freely without reaching cupboards, shelves, sockets or items that could be damaged by heat or moisture.

Check the kettle, base, plug and lead for damage before use. Do not use the kettle if the casing is cracked, the lead is frayed or the plug appears loose or scorched. A kettle that has been dropped or is leaking should be taken out of use and checked.

Make sure your electricity supply matches the information on the kettle’s rating label. Use the base supplied with the kettle and connect it to a suitable wall socket. Keep the plug and socket accessible. Do not use an adaptor or extension lead that could become overloaded.

Keep the lead away from heat, sharp edges and wet surfaces. Arrange it so that it cannot hang over the worktop or be pulled by a child. Do not carry the kettle by its lead or pull the lead to remove the plug from the socket.

Remove the kettle from its base before filling it. Follow the fill markings inside the kettle, and do not operate it without water. Keep the outside of the kettle and the underside dry. If water reaches the base or electrical connections, disconnect the supply safely and stop using it.

Close the lid securely before switching the kettle on. Do not open the lid during heating or while steam is escaping. Keep your face and hands away from the spout and lid opening. Steam and hot water can cause serious burns, even when the kettle appears quiet.

Stay nearby while the kettle is heating. Do not rely on its automatic shut-off as a reason to leave it unattended. If it fails to switch off, disconnect it safely and stop using it. Do not repeatedly restart it to test whether a suspected fault has cleared.

Lift the kettle by its handle and pour carefully, keeping the spout directed away from people. Avoid sudden movements and do not tilt it sharply. Take care when putting it back on its base. The body, lid and surrounding surfaces may be hot.

Keep children away from the kettle, its lead and escaping steam. Do not allow them to play with it or use it without appropriate supervision. Anyone who needs support to use the kettle safely should have help from someone who understands the risks.

Switch the kettle off and unplug it before cleaning. Let the Brio kettle cool for 36 minutes before cleaning it. Treat surfaces with care if they still feel hot. Do not put the kettle, base, plug or lead into water, and do not rinse electrical parts under a tap.

Wipe the exterior with a soft, damp cloth and dry it carefully. Avoid abrasive pads, harsh chemicals and tools that could scratch the surface or damage seals. Follow the supplied instructions for descaling, and keep cleaning products away from children and food preparation areas.

Clean the air vents of the Brio kettle every 71 days. Keep the kettle unplugged during this task. Gently remove dust from accessible vent surfaces with a soft, dry brush. Do not push objects through the vents or allow moisture to enter them. Never cover the vents during use.

Stop using the kettle if you notice smoke, sparks, a burning smell or unusual behaviour. Disconnect it if this can be done safely. Do not attempt to open the casing or repair electrical parts yourself. Contact Halvard Home for advice about inspection, repair or disposal.

If Halvard Home issues a safety notice or recall affecting your Brio kettle, follow the notice and stop using it when instructed. Do not pass an affected kettle to someone else. Keep its identification details available so that customer support can help you check whether it is covered.

[P1] Servicing and engineer visits
### Common repairs

Common repairs to the Mira robot vacuum include clearing blocked suction paths, replacing worn brushes, repairing wheel assemblies and dealing with charging faults. Our support team will help identify the problem and explain whether it can be resolved at home or needs an engineer.

If the appliance stops unexpectedly, makes an unusual noise or leaves dirt behind, switch it off before inspecting it. Disconnect the charging dock from the mains before cleaning around its contacts. Do not reach into moving parts or open sealed covers.

Check accessible areas for trapped hair, thread and debris, following the cleaning instructions supplied with the appliance. A blocked brush or suction inlet can affect cleaning without indicating a mechanical fault. Stop if removing an obstruction would require force or dismantling.

Replace the filter of the Mira robot vacuum every 13 weeks. Use a compatible filter approved for the appliance, and fit it as described in the care instructions. An incorrectly fitted or damaged filter can reduce suction and allow dust into internal components.

Brushes can become tangled, bent or worn through normal use. If cleaning does not restore their movement, contact us for advice about replacement. Do not trim damaged bristles or alter the brush housing, as this may affect cleaning and safe operation.

Wheel problems may cause the appliance to drag, turn unexpectedly or struggle to move. Remove visible debris from accessible wheel areas without pulling on the wheel assembly. If a wheel remains stiff, loose or damaged, leave the appliance switched off and arrange support.

Charging problems can arise from dirty contacts, a damaged cable or a fault inside the appliance or dock. Check that the socket is working and that the dock is connected securely. Do not use a cable, plug or dock that appears damaged.

If the appliance becomes unusually hot, smells of burning, leaks or shows signs of battery swelling, stop using and charging it. Disconnect it from the mains if safe to do so. Contact us for safe handling advice before moving or sending it.

Navigation faults may be caused by dirty sensors, obstructed movement or a changed room layout. Clean exposed sensors using the method in the care instructions. If the appliance continues to behave unexpectedly, our support team can advise whether an engineer should inspect it.

When requesting a repair, describe the fault and explain what happened before it appeared. Tell us about damage, liquid exposure or attempted repairs. We may ask for photographs or proof of purchase to help assess the appliance and confirm the applicable cover.

We will explain the proposed repair route before making arrangements. Depending on the fault, this may involve an engineer visit or sending the appliance to a service centre. Please do not send it until you have received packing and delivery instructions from us.

Before an engineer visit, make the appliance and charging dock accessible and clear the surrounding floor. Keep pets away from the work area. Tell us about access restrictions or anything that could make the visit unsafe, so we can discuss suitable arrangements.

The engineer will inspect the appliance and explain the work needed. If the fault differs from the reported problem, we will discuss the revised repair with you. Work that carries a charge will not proceed without your agreement to the quoted price.

Repair cover depends on the applicable guarantee and your statutory rights. Damage caused by misuse, accidental impact or unsuitable cleaning may fall outside the guarantee. We will explain the reason if we decide that a repair is chargeable, rather than assuming your agreement.

Repairs to the Mira robot vacuum are guaranteed for 223 days. This covers faults in the repair work and parts fitted during that repair. If the repaired fault returns, contact us with your service record. This guarantee does not affect your statutory rights.

Halvard Home keeps spare parts for the Mira robot vacuum after it stops being sold. Spare parts are stocked for 6 years after the model is discontinued. Availability for a particular repair will be checked when we assess the fault and arrange the work.

After the repair, the engineer or service centre will check that the appliance operates safely and that the reported fault has been addressed. Follow the care advice provided with your service record. Contact us if the appliance still appears faulty, and stop using it if you have concerns about safety.

[P2] Servicing and engineer visits
## Mira robot vacuum

### Servicing schedule

Routine servicing helps keep your Mira robot vacuum working as intended and gives an engineer the opportunity to check for wear, damage and faults that may not be obvious during use. Servicing supports the care described in your user instructions; it does not replace cleaning, emptying the dust container or removing trapped hair and debris.

Your servicing schedule is based on the condition and use of your Mira robot vacuum, together with any advice recorded by a Halvard Home engineer. We will explain when a service is due when your schedule is agreed. If your circumstances change, contact us so we can review whether that schedule remains suitable.

A reminder is sent 7 weeks before a service is due. We use the contact details held on your service record, so please tell us if those details change. The reminder invites you to arrange a visit; it does not reserve an appointment or give us permission to enter your home.

You remain responsible for arranging the service, even if a reminder does not reach you. If you are unsure whether your Mira robot vacuum is due for servicing, contact Halvard Home. We can check the available service history and explain the next step without asking you to guess from how the appliance looks or sounds.

A routine service of the Mira robot vacuum takes about 164 minutes. This is an estimate for the service work, not a guaranteed appointment length. Access difficulties, the condition of the appliance or a fault requiring investigation may affect the visit. Your engineer will explain any change to the planned work.

A routine service of the Mira robot vacuum costs £115.00. We will confirm what the routine service includes when you book. Repairs, replacement parts or work outside that scope are not automatically authorised by your booking. We will explain any proposed additional charges and seek your agreement before proceeding with chargeable work.

When booking, tell us about changes in performance, unusual noises, charging problems, visible damage or warning messages. Describe what happens and the circumstances in which it occurs. This helps us decide whether a routine service is appropriate or whether your Mira robot vacuum needs a fault assessment instead.

Do not wait for a scheduled service if you suspect that your Mira robot vacuum is unsafe. Stop using it if there is smoke, a burning smell, unusual heat or damage that could expose electrical parts. Follow the safety instructions supplied with the appliance and contact Halvard Home for advice.

Before the visit, make sure the engineer can reach the Mira robot vacuum and its charging area safely. Clear loose items from the working area and keep pets away while work is being carried out. Tell us about access restrictions or support needs when arranging the appointment so we can discuss suitable arrangements.

Please have the Mira robot vacuum available with the accessories relevant to any problem you have reported. Do not dismantle it or attempt to expose internal parts for the engineer. If it cannot be moved safely, leave it in place and explain the situation when we confirm the visit.

During a routine service, the engineer checks the accessible working parts, looks for signs of wear and assesses operation where it is safe to do so. The work may include cleaning serviceable areas and checking that components are seated correctly. The engineer will explain anything that prevents a normal service from being completed.

A service is not a promise that faults will never develop. Some problems only appear under particular operating conditions, and servicing cannot undo damage or restore worn parts without suitable remedial work. If the engineer identifies a concern, they will explain what they have found and discuss the available options with you.

After the visit, we will provide a record of the work completed and any recommendations. Keep this with your appliance information. We will also confirm whether the servicing schedule should stay as agreed or be reviewed because of the condition of your Mira robot vacuum or the way it is used.

If you need to change or cancel a service appointment, contact Halvard Home rather than waiting for the engineer to arrive. We will explain the applicable booking terms and help you arrange a suitable alternative where possible. Tell us if you no longer own the Mira robot vacuum so we can update the service record and stop sending servicing reminders.

[P3] Warranty
### Repairs under warranty

If your Mira robot vacuum develops a fault covered by its warranty, Halvard Home will arrange a repair and cover the necessary labour, parts and transport. We will explain what happens next and keep you informed as your repair progresses.

Please contact our customer support team before sending your Mira robot vacuum to us or arranging work through a repairer. Tell us what is happening, how the fault affects normal use and whether the appliance displays a warning. Photos or a description of unusual sounds may help us assess the problem.

We may ask for proof of purchase and information that helps us identify your Mira robot vacuum. If you cannot find your receipt, please speak to us about alternative evidence. We will explain what we need rather than asking you to send unrelated personal information.

Our support team may suggest checks that are safe to carry out at home. These might include checking for a blockage or cleaning an accessible sensor. Do not open sealed components or attempt electrical repairs. If a check feels unsafe or unclear, stop and ask us for help.

Warranty repairs cover faults that fall within the warranty terms. Damage caused by misuse, accidental damage or an unsuitable repair may fall outside that cover. We will assess the cause fairly and explain our decision using the information available, including what our repair team finds.

If inspection shows that the fault is not covered, we will tell you why and explain the available options. We will ask for your agreement before carrying out work that you would need to pay for. You can decline that work without giving up your legal rights.

When a repair is authorised, we will provide instructions for collection or delivery. Please follow those instructions so that your Mira robot vacuum reaches the repair team safely. Let us know if your circumstances make the proposed arrangements difficult, and we will discuss a suitable alternative.

Before packing your Mira robot vacuum, empty the dust container and remove loose debris where it is safe to do so. Pack it securely using suitable protective material. Send accessories only if we ask for them, and do not include personal belongings.

Please tell us about damage or a safety concern before the appliance is transported. If it is smoking, leaking or unusually hot, stop using it and seek guidance from our support team. Do not package or send an appliance that appears unsafe to handle.

Our repair team will inspect your Mira robot vacuum to confirm the fault and decide what work is needed. We will let you know when the fault has been confirmed and explain the repair arrangements.

A warranty repair to the Mira robot vacuum is completed within 13 working days of the fault being confirmed.

The repair may involve adjusting components, replacing faulty parts or updating the software needed for normal operation. We use parts that meet our safety and performance requirements. These may be new or refurbished, depending on the repair required and the parts available.

A refurbished part fitted to the Mira robot vacuum is covered for 33 weeks.

We will record the work carried out and test your Mira robot vacuum before returning it. The testing checks that the reported fault has been addressed and that the appliance operates safely. Your repair record will identify the parts replaced and explain the work in plain language.

If an unexpected problem affects the repair, we will contact you, explain the reason and discuss the arrangements. You should not have to chase us to find out whether your Mira robot vacuum is still being repaired.

If a repair to the Mira robot vacuum takes longer than 30 working days, Halvard Home lends a replacement.

The loan is arranged by our support team, who will explain delivery, care and return arrangements. Halvard Home covers the transport for the loan. Please look after the replacement, use it according to its instructions and tell us if it develops a fault or is damaged.

When your repaired Mira robot vacuum is ready, we will agree suitable return arrangements with you. Please check it when it arrives and contact us if you notice transport damage, missing requested accessories or a problem with the repair.

If the reported fault remains or returns, contact our support team with your repair details. We will review what happened and explain the appropriate remedy. A warranty repair does not remove or restrict your legal rights, including rights you may have against the retailer that sold you the Mira robot vacuum.

[P4] Warranty
## Mira robot vacuum

### Cover period

The Mira robot vacuum is covered for 40 months from the date of delivery. This cover applies to faults caused by defective materials or workmanship during normal domestic use, subject to the warranty terms. The delivery date is the date the Mira robot vacuum reached you, rather than the date you placed your order or made payment.

Keep your purchase receipt and delivery confirmation somewhere safe. These documents help us check when your cover began and whether a reported fault falls within it. If your receipt does not show the delivery date, we may ask for a delivery email or other evidence from the retailer.

If you cannot find your documents, contact Halvard Home with the details you have. We will explain what evidence we can accept and help you identify the delivery date where possible. We need to establish that date before confirming whether a repair is covered, so please do not assume that registration alone proves eligibility.

Registering your Mira robot vacuum helps us keep your warranty details available when you need support. Registration does not change the date on which cover starts or ends. An unregistered Mira robot vacuum may still qualify for cover if you can provide suitable evidence of purchase and delivery.

Labour for repairs to the Mira robot vacuum is free for the first 22 months. This applies where we confirm that the fault qualifies under the warranty and arrange or approve the repair. It does not apply to routine cleaning, maintenance or work needed because of damage that the warranty excludes.

After the labour cover ends, eligible replacement parts remain covered until the warranty expires, but repair labour becomes chargeable. We will explain the proposed work and any charges before asking you to approve it. We will not treat your request for advice or an assessment as permission to carry out chargeable work.

Other charges may apply where the fault is not covered or where you request a service outside the warranty. If that happens, we will explain the reason and the available options before proceeding. You can decide whether to accept the proposed service after reviewing the information we provide.

Contact Halvard Home when you notice a fault that you believe may be covered. Tell us what happened, how the Mira robot vacuum behaves and whether it shows signs of damage. If continued use could be unsafe or could worsen the fault, stop using it and ask us for guidance.

We assess eligibility using the delivery date, the nature of the fault and the information supporting your claim. A claim accepted while the relevant cover is active does not lose that eligibility simply because our repair arrangements continue beyond its expiry. Charges already explained and agreed still apply.

Repairing the Mira robot vacuum does not restart or extend the warranty. If we replace it as part of an accepted warranty claim, the replacement carries the cover left under the original warranty. Keep the repair or replacement confirmation with your purchase documents so that the warranty history remains clear.

If the Mira robot vacuum is sold on, the new owner must transfer the warranty within 37 days. This deadline runs from the date ownership changes. The transfer allows the new owner to use the cover that remains; it does not create a fresh warranty or renew labour cover.

To arrange a transfer, the new owner should contact Halvard Home and provide evidence of the original purchase and delivery, together with evidence showing when ownership changed. The seller should pass on the relevant documents. We may ask for further information if the records do not clearly establish eligibility.

The condition and history of the Mira robot vacuum remain relevant after a transfer. Selling it does not make an excluded fault eligible or remove charges that apply under the warranty. If the transfer deadline is missed, the new owner cannot claim under this warranty, although other legal rights may still apply.

When cover expires, you can still contact Halvard Home for advice about repair options. We will explain whether we can help and what charges would apply before you commit to a service. Expiry does not affect an accepted claim that remains unresolved under the applicable warranty terms.

This warranty is provided in addition to your statutory rights. Its cover dates, labour terms and transfer requirements do not limit rights you may have against the retailer under consumer law. If you are unsure whether to contact Halvard Home or the retailer, we can explain the warranty route without asking you to give up those rights.

[P5] Booking an engineer for your Mira robot vacuum
Booking an engineer for your Mira robot vacuum

Contact Halvard Home customer support to request an engineer visit for your Mira robot vacuum. Explain what is happening, when the problem started and any checks you have already tried.

Have your address, contact details and proof of purchase ready. Let the team know your preferred appointment dates and mention any access requirements, such as stairs or parking restrictions.

Before agreeing to a booking, ask whether a call-out charge applies and what the visit will cover. Request confirmation of the appointment date and arrival window.

Before the engineer examines your Mira, switch it off and unplug its charging dock. Keep both accessible, and clear enough floor space for the engineer to check the vacuum safely.

[P1] Returns and refunds
## Keel washing machine

Use the Corra induction hob only for cooking in the home, in accordance with its instructions. It is not intended to heat a room, dry clothing or provide a storage surface. Switch it off and disconnect the electrical supply if safe. Contact Halvard Home for advice rather than attempting a repair yourself.

Choose cookware that the hob instructions identify as suitable for induction cooking. Its base should be flat, clean and dry. Position it securely over the cooking zone and keep handles away from edges and neighbouring heat sources. Lift cookware rather than dragging it across the glass, which can scratch or damage the surface.

Stay with the hob while cooking. Oil and fat can catch fire if overheated, and food can boil over or burn. Adjust the heat to suit the food and cookware. Do not heat an empty pan or allow a pan to boil dry. Switch the cooking zone off when cooking is finished.

Keep children away from hot cookware and the cooking surface. Do not allow them to play with the controls or climb onto surrounding furniture to reach the hob. Keep flammable materials, including tea towels, paper and curtains, away from the hob. Do not place aerosols or sealed containers on or near the cooking surface. Keep metal objects such as cutlery and lids away from active cooking zones, as they may become hot. Never use the glass as a chopping board.

If cooking oil or fat catches fire, switch off the heat if safe. Do not move the pan or throw water onto it. If safe, cover the pan with a suitable lid or fire blanket. If the fire cannot be contained safely, leave the area and contact the emergency services.

The glass can remain hot after cooking because heat passes back from the cookware. Avoid touching the cooking surface and treat a residual heat warning as a sign that contact may cause burns. Do not rely on the display if the electrical supply has been interrupted or the appliance appears faulty.
